findings.title: Tab III re-mapped variants are scored against text projected with a different PCA basis
findings.problem: Each re-mapped variant (pixels, centre, legacy) is a separate run_mapping.py run, so it fits its own PCA basis. run_mapping.py never seeds torch, and StreamingPCA.accumulate keeps a random 20,000 of the 76,800 pixels per frame (unseeded torch.randperm). ablation_rows.row_factory loads only ck['field'] from the variant file and ignores ck['pca']. eval_seg.load_scene projects the text with the MAIN field's basis (line 256 from_state(ckpt['pca']), line 281 project_text). So the variant's mu* (64-d coordinates in its own basis) is dotted with text in another basis. Nothing checks that the two bases are equal.
findings.failure_scenario: The Tab III rows 'Pixels instead of views', 'Centered features' and 'Pixel-level variant' change the PCA basis as well as the part they claim to change. Columns whose sign flips or that rotate between the two fits get the wrong sign in the class score, so mIoU/ECE/NLL of these rows drop for a reason that has nothing to do with the ablation. 'Centered features' P0 should equal Full P0 exactly (same raw channel), but it will not.
findings.evidence: CPU proxy with the cached OpenCLIP tokens (not LSeg; GPU was off limits): two StreamingPCA fits on the same 20 Sequence_1 frames at 240x320 that differ only in the random subsample (scratchpad/pca_flip_idx.py, pca_cross_basis.py). office_0 seed 1 vs 2: 2 columns flip sign (57, 61). room_2 seed 1 vs 4: 7 columns flip (17, 19, 20, 41, 48, 60, 62) and 2 rotate. Accuracy of basis-B features scored with basis-B text vs basis-A text (what eval_seg does): office_0 0.6763 vs 0.6750; room_2 (seed 4) 0.7598 vs 0.7494 (-1.0 pt); room_2 (seed 5) 0.7597 vs 0.7568. The CPU default generator is seeded differently per process (torch.initial_seed() printed 963274053633879740 and then 14930468800794558177). PyTorch also seeds the CUDA default generator non-deterministically via getNonDeterministicRandom(is_cuda) (c10/core/GeneratorImpl.h:108), but I could not confirm this on the GPU here. The partial val log shows Tab I row differences of about 0.1 pt mIoU, so a basis effect up to 1 pt is as large as the effects Tab III measures.
findings.fix: Make the basis identical by construction. Add run_mapping.py --pca-from <main field>, which loads its pca basis (and zbar) and skips the fit, and use it in replica_tab3.sh (and in replica_views.sh for the k-view fields). In ablation_rows.row_factory, raise unless torch.equal(ck['pca']['basis'], main ckpt['pca']['basis']). Also seed run_mapping (torch.manual_seed, or pass a torch.Generator to accumulate) so fields can be reproduced.

findings.title: No pipeline produces the Tab III AUSE columns defined in the caption (e_red / e_irr averaged over 10/30/90-frame fields)
findings.where: papers/main.tex Table III caption (tab:ablation, 'AUSE: u_epi against e_red (epi) and u_ale against e_irr (ale), averaged over the 10-, 30- and 90-frame fields'); usplat/ablation_rows.py:3-5; scripts/replica_tab3.sh:103-128; scripts/replica_views.sh:52-60; scripts/eval_views.py:98-109; usplat/seg_eval.py:381-384
findings.problem: replica_tab3.sh builds only full-length variant fields and runs eval_seg.py. eval_seg's 'ranking' AUSE uses err = 1 - correct on the full map (seg_eval.py:381), which is AUSE against the 0/1 error, not against e_red or e_irr. The ablation_rows docstring says its P0 rows supply 'the AUSE columns'. No script builds k-view fields for any variant. replica_views.sh hard-codes --row-factory usplat.baselines:row_factory and --rows ours_P0,ours_P2,averaging,normlift,viewcount, and it deletes the k-view fields after each scene. eval_views.summarize reports per k. No code averages over k (grep for abl_/ablation_rows/views_test outside tests finds only replica_tab3.sh).
findings.failure_scenario: If the Tab III test run goes ahead as scripted, the only AUSE numbers for the variant rows are AUSE vs the 0/1 error on the 179-frame maps. Put under the caption's heading, they would be wrong. Computing the captioned quantity after the test run would need new k-view mappings (3 variants x 3 k x 6 test scenes) and a second pass over the test scenes. The views run would also already have deleted the main k-view fields that the read-out rows (est_rbar/joint/legacy) could reuse.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'abl_|ablation_rows|views_test|e_red' over scripts/ and usplat/ finds no consumer that combines ablation rows with k-view fields. replica_views.sh:53 fixes the baselines factory, and line 60 does rm -f of the k fields. replica_tab3.sh:118 runs eval_seg with the ablation factory on full fields only. eval_views.py:98-109 summarizes per k.
findings.fix: Decide before the Tab III test. Either (a) extend replica_views.sh: map k-view fields per re-mapped variant (<s>_lseg_k<k>_<v>.pt, with the main PCA), use a row factory that returns baseline rows plus ablation rows (read-out copies of the k-field plus <k-field>_<v>.pt), pass betas merged from the Tab I and Tab III val fits, and add a step that averages AUSE(u_epi, e_red) and AUSE(u_ale, e_irr) over k per scene, then over scenes. Run all of this before the k fields are deleted. Or (b) change the caption and text to the quantity the pipeline measures (AUSE vs the 0/1 error on the full map).

findings.title: Tab III 'Full method' temperatures will differ from Tab I 'Ours' because the 2D row shifts the fitter's random subsets
findings.where: scripts/eval_seg.py:390-400 (fit_on adds rows2d between scenes); usplat/seg_eval.py:446,466-469 (one seeded generator shared by all add calls); scripts/replica_tab1.sh:49 (--with-2d) vs scripts/replica_tab3.sh:118-120 (no --with-2d)
findings.problem: BetaFitter draws the per-view pixel subset (cap 2000) from one generator. In Tab I the 2D row's views of office_0 draw from it before room_2's 3D rows are added, so room_2 gets different subsets than in the Tab III fit, which has no 2D row. So the ours_* betas depend on whether an unrelated row is present.
findings.failure_scenario: In Tab III, 'Full method' ECE/NLL (and P2 parameters) will not match the Ours row of Tab I for the same field. A reader comparing the two tables sees two different numbers for one method.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/beta_2d_shift.py (toy CLI, two val scenes, --fit-pixels 50): ours_P0 beta 8.520 with the 2D row vs 9.826 without; P2 beta0 45.74 vs 36.51. With the real cap of 2000 the shift will be smaller but not zero.
findings.fix: Seed the subset per (scene, view), e.g. a generator seeded from hash(scene name, frame idx), or fit the 2D row with its own BetaFitter. Or have Tab III reuse the Tab I betas for the ours_* rows.

findings.title: Frame counts in the paper and figure differ from what the pose-gap filter keeps
findings.where: scripts/run_mapping.py:183-200 (select); papers/main.tex Setup ('every 5th frame of Sequence_1 (180 frames)') and fig:views ('M of the 180 mapping frames', M in {10,30,90})
findings.problem: select() drops a frame whose pose gap to the last kept frame is below 5 cm AND 5 deg. It applies this after the evenly spaced subset, so k is not always k, and the full map does not use 180 frames. The paper does not mention the filter.
findings.failure_scenario: The paper states 180 mapping frames for every method, and M=90 on the figure axis. The fields actually use 176-180 frames, and room_1's 90-frame field uses 89.
findings.evidence: Simulation of select() on the traj_w_c.txt poses (CPU): full map kept 179 (office_0, room_2, room_0, office_3), 178 (room_1, office_2), 176 (office_1), 180 (office_4). k=10 and k=30 are exact for all 8 scenes. k=90 gives 89 for room_1. This agrees with the map logs: 'keyframes used 179' for office_0 and room_2.
findings.fix: Write '180 frames, minus near-duplicate poses (at most 4 per scene)' in Setup, or set --kf-trans 0 for Replica. For the figure, subsample after the filter so k is exact, or plot the recorded n_mapping_views.

findings.title: k-view fields do not share the full field's PCA basis exactly, which adds basis noise to e_red
findings.problem: Each k-view field fits its own PCA on the same 20 frames, but with an unseeded random subsample. eval_views stays internally consistent (each field projects its text with its own basis, eval_seg.py:256,281). But a pixel can flip between right and wrong because of the basis alone, and that pixel is then counted as e_red or dropped from e_irr.
findings.failure_scenario: A small share of e_red / e_irr pixels comes from PCA sampling noise, not from the number of views. This matters most at k=90, where e_red is smallest.
findings.evidence: CPU proxy (scratchpad/pca_seed_effect.py, OpenCLIP tokens): labels changed on 0.141% (office_0) and 0.111% (room_2) of pixels between two fits, and correctness flipped on 0.073% / 0.069%.
findings.fix: Same as the first finding: map the k-view fields with the full field's basis (--pca-from). In eval_views, assert that the k-field and full-field bases are equal.

findings.title: The views figure's M=180 point (e_irr column) is not produced by replica_views.sh
findings.where: scripts/replica_views.sh:18 (KS='10 30 90'); papers/main.tex fig:views placeholder ('plus M=180 in the e_irr column')
findings.problem: The pipeline makes no 180 point. At M=180, e_irr equals the 0/1 error on covered pixels. So the value equals the Tab I eval JSON summary[row]['covered']['ause'][channel], which uses the same pixel set and the same three-tier key. Nothing documents or extracts it.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever draws the figure has to find the M=180 value by hand, or map a duplicate 'k=180' field for no reason.
findings.evidence: seg_eval.summarize (covered variant, err = 1 - correct, ranking_signals on covered pixels) and views_cross_ause (covered in both maps, identical geometry) select the same pixels and keys.
findings.fix: Take the M=180 point from the Tab I test JSON ('covered' variant) in the figure script, and note this in the eval_views docstring.

findings.title: Ablation rows exist only for P0 and P2, but the paper leaves the full method's predictive open (P0, P1 or P2)
findings.where: usplat/ablation_rows.py:65-70; papers/main.tex sec:ablation ('The full method uses \todo{the predictive chosen on validation (P0, P1 or P2 ...)}')
findings.problem: variant_rows builds abl_<v>_P0 and abl_<v>_P2 (P2 on the P0 buffer) only.
findings.failure_scenario: If validation picks P1 (it has the best office_0 mIoU in the partial log, 0.3011), the Tab III variant rows cannot use the same predictive as the Full row. The table would then change two things per row.
findings.evidence: eval_val_partial_2013.log: ours_P1 mIoU 0.3011 vs P0/P2 0.3002; P2 has the best ECE/NLL.
findings.fix: Fix the choice (P2) in the text now, or add abl_<v>_P1 rows (FieldRow mode='P1') before the Tab III val fit.

findings.title: The stage guards check that eval_val.json exists, not that the val run succeeded
findings.problem: usplat.runlog writes the record at start (status 'running') and on failure (status 'failed', metrics {}). '[ -f eval_val.json ]' passes in both cases.
findings.failure_scenario: A test stage started after a failed or unfinished val run maps every test field or k-view field (hours of GPU time), then crashes in eval with 'no usable fitted beta'. No wrong number comes out, but the gap between shared-GPU jobs is wasted.
findings.evidence: The current /home/thanhnc/gauss_ws/data/uags_results/tab1/eval_val.json exists with status 'failed' and metrics {} (OOM at 20:16:31).
findings.fix: Guard with python3 -c "import json,sys; sys.exit(json.load(open(p)).get('status','ok')!='ok')" (plain-json files have no status).

findings.title: replica_tab3.sh hides the mapping log when a variant mapping fails
findings.problem: Under set -e, a failing gpu_gate/run_mapping command at line 110 ends the script at once. The '|| { tail ...; }' is attached to the grep on line 114, not to the mapping command, unlike in replica_tab1.sh and replica_views.sh.
findings.failure_scenario: An OOM or crash while mapping a variant exits with no message on the console.
findings.evidence: Lines 110-113 have no '||' after the redirect.
findings.fix: Append '|| { tail -20 "$OUT/map_${s}_${v}.log"; exit 1; }' to the gpu_gate command.

checked_ok: Tests pass on CPU: tests/test_ablation_rows.py + test_state.py + test_change.py (16 passed); test_seg_eval.py -k views (2 passed); test_seg_eval.py + test_estimators.py + test_legacy.py + test_baselines.py (45 passed).

replica_views.sh deletes the k-view fields only after eval_views.py exits 0. eval_views writes its JSON (eval_views.py:152-154) before it returns, and on failure the script exits before the rm (lines 52-60).

k-view mapping flags match the Tab I mapping (stride 5, downscale 2, --pca-frames 20, --feat-dim 64, lseg, --baselines). change_test=false changes no read-out: with no update sequence, change_thr stays inf and nothing resets.

PCA frames: run_mapping fits PCA on the first 20 stride-5 frames of ds before select(), so every k uses the same frames. Each field's text is projected with that field's own basis in eval_views, so each k is internally consistent (see the basis-noise finding for the remaining gap).
--max-keyframes: evenly spaced torch.linspace subset, then the pose-gap filter. Simulated on the real poses: k=10 and k=30 are exact on all 8 scenes. k=90 is exact except room_1 (89).

e_red = wrong at k AND right at full, e_irr = wrong at both, on pixels covered in both maps (views_cross_ause covered_only). Arrays are aligned by the same frame order and checked by GT equality. The uncovered set is the same at every k (shared geometry, alpha does not depend on the field). This matches the paper's metrics text.

The Tab III 'Pixels instead of views' mapping config, printed from replica_tab3.sh's own one-liner: {evidence: pixels, epistemic: pixels, change_test: false}. centre: {centre: true, change_test: false}. legacy: FieldConfig.legacy() with change_test false (readmit_depth set to None by run_mapping without --use-depth).

est_legacy = clamp(r_bar - (1 - r_bar)/(W1 + 1)), the paper's r_tilde with W1. est_rbar = ||R||/W1. est_joint = ||R||/(W1 + c0). u_epi is unchanged for all read-out variants. u_ale definedness is the same as for kish (support >= tau_min implies W1^2 - W2 > 0).
Temperatures are refit for every ablation row on val (replica_tab3.sh STAGE=val runs eval_seg --val-scenes with the ablation factory). The P2 ablation rows use the P0 buffer, like ours_P2.

state_dict saves None only for tensors that start at zero. NaN-initialised tensors (c_ring, c_last, depth_last) are always saved. A round trip through torch.save/load gives identical frozen rows and state for the tab1, views-k, pixels, centre and legacy configs (my script output: True for all 5).

calib_mode shim: calib_names=2 was added in the same commit as the rename (4829617), so only states saved before the rename map 'pooled' to 'history'. calibrate_change_threshold 'pooled' now sets one flat threshold and stops recording.

NormLift 1 - C_inter = 1 - ||sum_v R_v|| / sum_v ||R_v||, which is the paper's C_inter = ||f|| / C_intra. The views rows (ours_P0, ours_P2, averaging, normlift, viewcount) provide every reference curve the figure text names.
The M=180 e_irr value equals the Tab I 'covered' variant AUSE of the same channel (same pixels, same three-tier key).
